exposure: Angle of progression measured via midsagittal transperineal ultrasound
Angle of progression measured via parasagittal transperineal ultrasound
outcome: Inter-method agreement between midsagittal and parasagittal angle of progression measurements
Correlation between angle of progression measurements and mode of delivery
Correlation between angle of progression measurements and duration of the active second stage of labor
cohort: 151 women in active labor with a singleton uncomplicated term pregnancy with fetuses in vertex presentation
finding: There was excellent agreement between midsagittal and parasagittal angle of progression measurements, although parasagittal measurements tended to overestimate the angle.
mod_finding: The angle of progression measured by either method was significantly wider in patients who delivered vaginally compared to those who had a cesarean section.
